This brochure provides information about the qualifications and business practices of Thornwood Capital Advisors, LLC. If you have any questions about the contents of this brochure, please contact us at (617) 555-0181 or compliance@thornwoodcapital.com. The information in this brochure has not been approved or verified by the United States Securities and Exchange Commission or by any state securities authority.

Additional information about Thornwood Capital Advisors, LLC is available on the SEC's website at www.adviserinfo.sec.gov.

Registration as an investment adviser does not imply a certain level of skill or training.

Item 2. Material Changes

Since the annual updating amendment filed on March 30, 2025, we have made the following material change: effective January 1, 2026, we reduced our maximum annual advisory fee for separately managed accounts from 1.25% to 1.00% of assets under management, and we removed the performance-based fee option previously offered to qualified clients.

Item 4. Advisory Business

Thornwood Capital Advisors, LLC ("Thornwood", "we", or "us") is a Massachusetts limited liability company formed in 2011 and registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission as an investment adviser. Our principal owners are Elaine Thornwood-Reyes (62%) and Samuel Okafor (38%).

We provide discretionary and non-discretionary investment management to individuals, high-net-worth individuals, trusts, estates, and charitable organizations. We tailor advice to each client's stated objectives, time horizon, liquidity needs, and risk tolerance, which we document in an investment policy statement at the start of the relationship and review at least annually. A client may impose reasonable restrictions on investing in specific securities or types of securities.

As of December 31, 2025, we managed $1,184,300,000 in discretionary assets and $96,700,000 in non-discretionary assets.

Item 5. Fees and Compensation

Our annual advisory fee for separately managed accounts is 1.00% of assets under management on the first $5,000,000, 0.75% on the next $10,000,000, and 0.55% above $15,000,000. Fees are negotiable. We calculate the fee on the average daily balance of the account for the quarter and bill it quarterly in arrears. With the client's written authorization in the advisory agreement, we deduct fees directly from the client's custodial account; otherwise we invoice the client, and payment is due within 30 days.

A client may terminate the advisory agreement at any time on written notice, and we will refund any prepaid, unearned fee on a pro rata basis. Either party may terminate without penalty within five business days after the agreement is signed.

Our fees do not include brokerage commissions, transaction fees, custodial fees, wire fees, or the internal expenses of mutual funds and exchange-traded funds, which are described in each fund's prospectus. Item 12 describes our brokerage practices.

Neither we nor any of our supervised persons accepts compensation for the sale of securities or other investment products, including asset-based sales charges or service fees from the sale of mutual funds.

Item 6. Performance-Based Fees and Side-by-Side Management

We do not charge performance-based fees and we do not manage any account on a side-by-side basis with a performance-fee account.

Item 7. Types of Clients

We provide investment advice to individuals, high-net-worth individuals, trusts, estates, and charitable organizations. Our minimum account size is $500,000, which we may waive in our discretion, including for family members of existing clients and for accounts we expect to grow to the minimum within a reasonable period.

Item 8. Methods of Analysis, Investment Strategies and Risk of Loss

We use fundamental analysis, quantitative screening, and asset-allocation modeling. Our principal strategies are diversified global equity, core fixed income, and a tax-managed balanced strategy for taxable accounts.

Investing in securities involves risk of loss that clients should be prepared to bear. Principal risks include market risk, interest-rate risk, credit risk, inflation risk, liquidity risk, concentration risk, foreign and emerging-market risk, and the risk that our analysis or models prove incorrect. Past performance is not indicative of future results, and we do not guarantee any level of return.

Item 9. Disciplinary Information

We have no legal or disciplinary events that are material to a client's or prospective client's evaluation of our advisory business or the integrity of our management.

Item 10. Other Financial Industry Activities and Affiliations

Neither we nor any of our management persons is registered, or has an application pending to register, as a broker-dealer, a registered representative of a broker-dealer, a futures commission merchant, a commodity pool operator, or a commodity trading advisor. We have no arrangement that is material to our advisory business with a related person.

Item 11. Code of Ethics, Participation or Interest in Client Transactions and Personal Trading

We have adopted a code of ethics under Rule 204A-1 of the Investment Advisers Act of 1940 that requires our supervised persons to place client interests first, to report personal securities transactions and holdings quarterly and annually, to obtain preclearance for transactions in initial public offerings and limited offerings, and to comply with applicable federal securities laws. We will provide a copy of the code of ethics to any client or prospective client on request.

We do not buy or sell for our own accounts the same securities we recommend to clients, other than through pooled vehicles that hold broad market exposure. Our chief compliance officer reviews personal trading reports quarterly.

Item 12. Brokerage Practices

We recommend that clients custody assets at Fairhaven Trust Company. We select broker-dealers on the basis of execution quality, commission rates, financial responsibility, and responsiveness. We do not participate in soft-dollar arrangements, we do not receive research or other products in exchange for directing client transactions, and we do not receive client referrals from any broker-dealer or third party in exchange for directing brokerage.

We may aggregate orders for more than one client account. Where we aggregate, each participating account receives the average price and pays its pro rata share of transaction costs.

Item 13. Review of Accounts

Each account is reviewed at least quarterly by the portfolio manager assigned to it and by our chief investment officer. We review more frequently on a client's request, a significant deposit or withdrawal, or a material change in market conditions or the client's circumstances. Clients receive a quarterly written report from us and at least quarterly account statements directly from the custodian.

Item 14. Client Referrals and Other Compensation

We do not receive economic benefit from any person who is not a client for providing investment advice. We do not compensate any person, directly or indirectly, for client referrals.

Item 15. Custody

We do not maintain physical custody of client assets. We are deemed to have custody of client assets solely because clients authorize us to deduct our advisory fee directly from their custodial accounts. Clients receive account statements at least quarterly directly from Fairhaven Trust Company, and we urge clients to compare those statements with the reports we provide.

Item 16. Investment Discretion

Clients grant us discretionary authority in the advisory agreement and in the custodian's limited power of attorney. That authority permits us to determine the securities to be bought or sold and the amount, subject to any written restrictions the client imposes.

Item 17. Voting Client Securities

We vote proxies for client securities unless the client retains that authority in writing. We vote in the client's best economic interest under written proxy-voting policies, and we address any material conflict by voting in accordance with the recommendation of an independent proxy adviser. Clients may obtain our proxy-voting policies and a record of how we voted their securities by contacting compliance@thornwoodcapital.com.

Item 18. Financial Information

We do not require or solicit prepayment of more than $1,200 in fees per client six months or more in advance, and we are not aware of any financial condition reasonably likely to impair our ability to meet contractual commitments to clients. We have not been the subject of a bankruptcy petition at any time during the past ten years.
